key_insight: ReScene4D defines and benchmarks temporally sparse 4D semantic instance segmentation: maintaining consistent object instance identities across intermittently captured indoor 3D scans, even when objects move, appear, or disappear between observations.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of joint segmentation, identification, and long-range temporal association of object instances in evolving indoor scenes captured intermittently, where changes can be unobserved for extended intervals and standard 3D SIS methods fail to preserve identity consistency.
method: Formalize the temporally sparse 4D SIS task and introduce ReScene4D — a benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol tailored for intermittent captures and evolving indoor scenes.

Design a temporally-aware pipeline that combines robust per-scan 3D instance segmentation with a long-range association module (spatio-temporal features, matching, and memory) to link instances across gaps and occlusions.
Introduce evaluation metrics and baselines to measure semantic accuracy and identity consistency over time, emphasizing robustness to appearance/disappearance and sparse sampling.
impact: Provides a standardized task, dataset, and evaluation for temporally consistent instance-level scene understanding, enabling improvements in long-term 3D perception for robotics, AR/VR, and multi-view mapping where intermittent captures and scene dynamics are common.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing intermittent 3D scans with color-coded instance IDs that persist despite objects moving, appearing, and disappearing.

paper_title: ReScene4D: Temporally Consistent Semantic Instance Segmentation of Evolving Indoor 3D Scenes
paper_authors: Emily Steiner, Jianhao Zheng, Henry Howard-Jenkins, Chris Xie, Iro Armeni
